title: Enterprise Onboarding: Integration, Escalation, Health Checks & QBR Playbook
author: Asha Patel
content:
Summary:
This playbook consolidates the standard operating procedures, checklists, escalation paths, known issues and workarounds, and QBR/health-check templates used by Customer Success and Support for enterprise onboarding at Redwood Inference. It is intended for CSMs, Solutions Engineers, Support L2/L3, SRE, and Account stakeholders.

Purpose and scope:
- Purpose: Ensure predictable, repeatable, and low-risk onboarding for enterprise customers integrating Redwood API, Dedicated, or Private deployments.
- Scope: Covers technical integration checklist, escalation matrix & SLAs, routine health checks, QBR agenda & artifacts, and common known issues with workarounds and ownership. Applies to all enterprise onboarding engagements (post-contract signature).

Owner & stakeholders:
- Playbook owner: Customer Success (CSM guild)
- Primary stakeholders: CSM, Solutions Engineering (SE), Support Engineering (L2/L3), SRE, Product (integration), Account Executive (AE)
- Escalation contacts: see Escalation Matrix section below

Onboarding phases (high level):
1) Pre-kickoff (preparations)
   - Deliver: Onboarding plan, technical intake form, kickoff invite (owner: CSM).
   - Collect: API usage estimates, expected throughput/latency targets, VPC requirements (if private), data residency constraints, and security questionnaire.
2) Kickoff (0-7 days)
   - Attendees: CSM, SE, customer tech lead, customer security lead, AE (optional).
   - Agenda: objectives, timeline, success criteria, staging vs prod topology, ownership.
3) Integration (1-6 weeks depending on scope)
   - Activities: API key provisioning, auth & RBAC setup, model selection & config (quantization profile if applicable), network/VPC peering, sample workload tests, telemetry validation.
   - Deliverables: integration checklist completed, first successful end-to-end test.
4) Validation & performance tuning (1-3 weeks)
   - Activities: benchmark representative workload (99th pct latency, throughput), tune batching/caching/kv-cache policies, set alert thresholds.
   - Deliverables: SLOs agreed, performance baseline recorded in Redwood Console dashboards.
5) Launch & handoff (go-live)
   - Activities: final rollout plan (canary/gradual ramp), runbook handed to customer success & support, escalation points confirmed.
6) Post-launch (30-90 days)
   - Activities: Weekly check-ins (first month), SLA monitoring, QBR preparation (month 1 and quarterly thereafter).

Integration checklist (technical):
- Account & access:
  - Create enterprise API key(s) scoped for environment (staging/prod).
  - Configure RBAC roles in Redwood Console for customer SREs and devs.
- Networking & security:
  - Validate IP allowlists or configure VPC peering (Private deployments).
  - Confirm KMS/HSM integration for Private (if required) and key rotation policy.
- Model & runtime configuration:
  - Confirm model family and pinned version (e.g., open-llama-v2-13b-q5, redwood-verified-7b).
  - Apply quantization profile if requested (see quantization-profiles page).
  - Decide on streaming vs chunked responses for chat use-cases.
- Performance & cost optimization:
  - Set recommended batching max_tokens and timeout policy based on expected request distribution.
  - Enable prefix/KV caching for consistent prompts.
- Observability & alerts:
  - Add customer-specific dashboards to Redwood Console: token cost, 99th/50th latency, error rate, throughput.
  - Configure alerts: error_rate > 1% sustained for 5m, 99th latency > SLO, token cost drift > 20% vs baseline.
- Validation tests:
  - End-to-end smoke test (sample prompt sets).
  - Load test with representative concurrency (using perf-suite scripts).
  - Security scan for unredacted PII in logs (if required).

Sample config table (include in integration packet):
| Field | Example value | Required |
| API key (env) | REDWOOD_API_KEY=acct-prod-XXXX | yes |
| Model | open-llama-v2-13b-q5 | yes |
| Batch size (max_tokens) | 8 | recommended |
| KV cache | enabled | recommended |
| Region | us-west-2 | required for latency-sensitive workloads |

Escalation matrix & SLAs (enterprise):
- Severity definitions and targets (Customer-facing SLA targets when under enterprise support agreement):
  - P0 (Production down / data loss / system integrity): initial response 15 min, L1 remediation start 30 min, L2/SRE engaged 1 hour, resolution target 4 hours (exec updates every 60 mins).
  - P1 (Severe degradation, major feature non-functional): initial response 1 hour, L2 start 2 hours, resolution target 24 hours.
  - P2 (Partial loss or significant impact to workflow): initial response 4 hours, resolution target 3 business days.
  - P3 (Low impact / feature request / question): initial response 1 business day, resolution target 10 business days.
- Escalation path (ordered):
  1. CSM -> Support L2 (support-enterprise@redwood.ai) -> Support L3 / SE -> SRE -> Product Eng -> Exec escalation.
  2. For security incidents, contact security-oncall@redwood.ai and follow Security Incident Response doc.
- Communication channels:
  - Primary: Slack channel (customer-specific private channel) and email.
  - Pager: PagerDuty schedule for Support L2 and SRE on-call.
  - Status page: post incident updates to status.redwood.ai for P0/P1 incidents.

Contact matrix (example):
- CSM: Asha Patel (asha@redwood.ai)
- Support L2 lead: Miguel Reyes (miguel@redwood.ai)
- Solutions Engineering: Emily Chen (emily@redwood.ai)
- SRE oncall: see PagerDuty schedule (SRE Team)

Known issues and recommended workarounds (living list):
1) Intermittent 504s for streaming responses under specific client keepalive settings
   - Symptoms: client receives 504 when streaming connection is idle > 60s then resumes.
   - Root cause: intermediate load balancer idle timeout < client keepalive.
   - Workaround: set client keepalive to 30s or configure ALB idle timeout to 120s. Owner: eng-infra.
2) Elevated token cost after model switch (unexpected cost delta)
   - Symptoms: token cost per request spikes 2-3x vs baseline after pinning new model.
   - Root cause: model has larger context window / different tokenization behavior.
   - Workaround: adjust per-route token limits, enable response truncation, or revert to previous model while analyzing. Owner: product + CSM.
3) Private deployment: KMS key rotation breaks agent replication
   - Symptoms: failed key unwrap operations during replica sync.
   - Root cause: stale key reference in onprem configuration.
   - Workaround: follow onprem-packaging/upgrade-and-rollback checklist to re-sync and rotate keys carefully; open support ticket and tag security. Owner: eng-private-deployments.
4) High 99th percentile latency for chat workloads during steady-state
   - Symptoms: 99th latency > SLO, throughput normal.
   - Root cause: suboptimal batch window configuration under long-tail prompt length.
   - Workaround: enable dynamic batch shaping, reduce max_batch_latency_ms for the route and enable per-client batching heuristics. Owner: eng-serving-runtime + SE.

Known issues table (CSV snippet for quick copy):

Incident triage & runbook snippets:
- Immediate triage checklist (first 30 minutes):
  1. Record incident in incident tracker and create Slack incident channel.
  2. Capture scope: impacted customers, services, endpoints, regions.
  3. Collect logs: request/response ids, error traces, perf metrics.
  4. Apply mitigations: traffic re-routing, scale up Dedicated pool, enable fallback model variant.
  5. Communicate to customer (via CSM) every 30-60 minutes for P0.

- Example mitigation commands (internal CLI):
  - Force failover to fallback model: redwoodctl route fallback --customer acct-123 --route chat --model redwood-verified-7b
  - Increase Dedicated pool size: redwoodctl capacity scale --pool reserved-acct-123 --replicas 4

Health checks and QBR materials:
- Weekly health-check (CSM cadence):
  - Metrics reviewed: 7-day average token usage, 99th/50th latency, error rate, retries, cost per 1k tokens.
  - Actions: identify anomalies, open action items for SE/Support, schedule remediation.
- 30/60/90 day QBR template (quarterly thereafter):
  - Executive summary: adoption, value delivered, major incidents, risk profile.
  - Usage & performance: token growth, latencies, cost trends, top routes.
  - Reliability & incidents: P0-P3 summary, root causes, remediation progress.
  - Roadmap & initiatives: planned model upgrades, Dedicated capacity changes, private deployment milestones.
  - Action items & owners: clear next steps and due dates.

Attachments & artifacts to include with QBR:
- Redwood Console export of dashboards (CSV/PNG)
- Performance baseline run results (perf-suite JSON)
- Completed integration checklist (signed off)
- Incident RCA summaries since last QBR

Operational hygiene & review cadence:
- Playbook review: every 6 months (owner: CSM).
- Runbook drills: SRE & Support run through P0 tabletop every quarter.
- QBR cadence: monthly for first 3 months post-go-live, then quarterly.

Appendix: escalation contact templates (copy into customer Slack/email):
- Initial P0 message (Slack):
  "P0 - Production outage impacting <service>. Customer: <acct>. Start: <timestamp>. Impact: <short description>. Initial mitigation: <steps taken>. Owners: @CSM @Support-L2 @SRE-oncall. Details: <link to incident doc>."

- Email escalation template for exec update:
  Subject: [P0] <Customer> - <Service> outage - <HH:MM UTC>
  Body: Summary, scope, current mitigation steps, ETA for next update, primary contacts.
